statements.subject: session
statements.description: An RTSP agent SHALL NOT use more than one connection per RTSP session at any given point.
statements.guard_semantics: At most one TCP connection per RTSP session may be active at any given point in time

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the client has discovered that the TCP connection has been lost, it can set up a new one when there is need to communicate again.
statements.trigger: TCP connection loss detected & new communication needed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server that attempts to send a request to a client that has no connection currently to the server SHALL discard the request.
statements.trigger: server attempts to send request to client

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When under attack, an RTSP agent can close TCP connections and release state associated with that TCP connection.
actions: release state associated with TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A persistent connection MAY be closed after a few message exchanges. Later, when the client wishes to send a new request, a new connection would be opened.
statements.trigger: client wishes to send new request after persistent connection closed

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To avoid deadlock situations, both client and server MUST be able to send and receive requests simultaneously.
statements.guard_semantics: Endpoint must support concurrent send and receive to avoid deadlock
